column3: “Before the Father” renders “with the Father.”
“Atoning sacrifice” renders ἱλασμός (“propitiation”); BSB adds “the sins of” before “the whole world.”
“We can be sure” renders “we know.”
“I know Him” renders the perfect “I have known Him.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB has “Jesus” where the Greek has ἐκεῖνος (“that one”); “must” renders “ought.”
BSB follows the critical text with no “from the beginning” at the end; it leaves out “old” in the second clause and renders “the word” as “the message.”
“Then again” renders “again”; BSB adds “also” twice. “Is fading” renders “is passing away.”
“Still” renders “until now.”
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
BSB includes here “I have written to you, children, because you know the Father,” which the Greek counts as the start of verse 14.
BSB begins this verse with “fathers”; the sentence to the children stands in verse 13.
Close to the Greek.
“Pride of life” renders ἀλαζονεία (“boastful pride”).
Close to the Greek.
“Have appeared” renders “have come to be”; “this is how” renders ὅθεν (“whence”).
“Did not belong to us” renders “were not of us”; “their departure made it clear that none of them belonged to us” recasts “but so that it might be made manifest that they all are not of us.”
BSB follows the critical text with “all of you know”; BSB adds “the truth.” The Textus Receptus has “you know all things.”
“You lack knowledge of the truth” renders “you do not know the truth.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB includes the second clause, as the critical text does; it is absent from the Textus Receptus.
BSB shortens “if what you have heard from the beginning abides in you” to “if it does.”
Close to the Greek.
“Are trying to deceive you” renders “are leading you astray.”
“His true and genuine anointing” recasts “His anointing … is true and is not a lie”; BSB leaves out “and just as it has taught you.”
BSB has “Christ” where the Greek has “Him”; “be confident” renders “have boldness.”
Close to the Greek.
